transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being on this call. As we plan the memorial planting for Grandma, I'd like to go around the circle and hear from each of you about what you think should shape our decisions — things like location, tree choice, timing, the plaque, anything that's on your mind. I'll take all your input and then make the final plan. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have something important to share. I found a handwritten note from Grandma. In it, she asks for a serviceberry tree, and she specifies that the plaque should read exactly: 'For everyone who made room for joy.' I haven't shown it to anyone yet, but I think we should honor her wishes.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have something important to share too. I paid for a soil test of the backyard, and the report came back saying the yard drains poorly. Because of that, the planting bed must be raised exactly 20 centimeters above the surrounding soil. I hadn't shared the report yet, but I think we need to factor this into our planning, especially when it comes to choosing the location and preparing the site.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have something to share too. I get severe headaches from cedar mulch, so I can only take part in the planting if the bed uses cedar-free mulch. I haven't mentioned this to Nora yet, but I think it's important to factor into the materials plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have something to share too. I spoke with the arborist who'll be helping us with the planting, and he strongly recommended the east lawn for the location. He said the west patio edge is too close to the foundation, and the south fence strip is too narrow for the tree once it matures. I hadn't passed this along to anyone yet, but I think it's really important for deciding where to plant.
transcript.speaker: A5
